1.tell: Essay-author-attitude item: the only option that is a criticism of the advertised claim. A/B/D all endorse or half-endorse the method, and an essayist quoted as evaluating 'working methods' is set up to puncture an absolute marketing claim ('photographic reproduction'). C also names the general principle rather than a passage-specific excuse (D's 'Sarto face withdrawn early' reads like a distractor built from a stray detail).

2.tell: 'Effective power' signals the informal lever, not the formal one. C (go to court) is the nominal/legal route the phrasing is contrasting against; A is too sweeping for a market board; B (revoke the inherited pitch) is the nuclear option passages usually explicitly deny. D is the small, oddly concrete relocation ('thin end of the fourth block') — the kind of specific-but-minor detail that gets quoted as the real threat.

3.tell: Only option that supplies a mechanism linking the cited evidence (even spacing) to a cause; even spacing is the classic signature of territorial competition. B is a negative claim spacing cannot establish, C explains distribution not regularity, D is a duration claim spacing has nothing to do with.

4.tell: Narrative motive item: the key is the interior, characterising reason phrased as a reversal ('a day that asked nothing of her care was harder than a hard crossing'), not the practical ones (A perceptual, C skill-progress, D social embarrassment). Also the only option not tied to a checkable surface fact.
